dataset: Military credential recommender: USAF / ANG civilian credentials
method: Every fact was read from the cited official or primary source on the date checked. Fields that could not be read from an official source are 'UNVERIFIED'. AF COOL credential pages (afvec.us.af.mil) and DoD COOL USAF pages could not be reached from this network, so NO credential-to-AFSC mapping in this file comes from AF COOL. Mappings are either from the official AF Career Field Education and Training Plan (CFETP) for that AFSC, or marked 'inferred, not from AF COOL'.

af_cool.name: Air Force Credentialing Opportunities On-Line (AF COOL)

what_it_is.value: "The Air Force Credentialing Opportunities On-Line (AF COOL) program provides opportunities for enlisted members of the Air Force and Space Force to earn industry recognized professional credentials and licenses. The program is part of the Air Force Virtual Education Center."
what_it_is.source_note: Text read from a PDF print of the official myAirForceBenefits fact sheet (Regular Air Force: Active Duty version, 'Document Review Date: 10 October 2024') hosted at https://guard.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/AF-COOL-Benefit-Fact-Sheet-compressed.pdf. The .us.af.mil host itself did not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN) from this network.

what_it_funds.value: "The AF will pay for the exam(s), books (NTE $500), administrative/application fees, and recertification fees necessary for that one credential." Categories: Primary AFSC; leadership and management credentials for E-7 to E-9; "one non-AFSC related credential and one completed degree-associated credential, bachelor's or higher." "If a member fails the credential exam(s), they will be required to repay the cost of the credential."
what_it_funds.conflict: A 460th Force Support Squadron AF COOL trifold (PDF created 2024-07-05, https://www.460fss.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/AF-COOL-Tri-Fold.pdf) says it 'Covers books, coursework, prep courses, exams, admin fees, and recurring re-certifications.' The fact sheet lists only exams, books, admin/application fees and recertification. Treat prep course/coursework coverage as UNVERIFIED.

funding_cap.quote: "Funding will not exceed a maximum of $4,500 per lifetime per Air and Space professional."
funding_cap.source_url: https://guard.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/AF-COOL-Benefit-Fact-Sheet-compressed.pdf (copy of myairforcebenefits.us.af.mil fact sheet, review date 10 October 2024)
funding_cap.corroborated_by: https://www.460fss.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/AF-COOL-Tri-Fold.pdf ('$4,500 AF COOL Lifetime Cap Allowance (maximum of $500 per goal for study material/book(s))')

general_eligibility.quote: "Possess a 5-skill level in their Primary AFSC; Do not have an Unfavorable Information File (UIF), are not on a Control Roster, and are current on their most recent Fitness test at the time of application; Have a profile in AFVEC with an approved credentialing goal; Must obtain supervisor approval and complete the entire credential while on active duty status"

ang_eligibility.summary: ANG members are eligible only while on qualifying active orders (Title 10, or Title 32 section 502(f)) for the entire credential process. Drill status alone does not qualify (per search-indexed text of the official ANG fact sheet; see verification note).
ang_eligibility.quote_opened_source: "*ANG and AFRS must be on Title 10 or Title 32, Section (502)F Orders for entire duration of credential process." and "Air National Guard and Air Force Reserve members are eligible to utilize AF COOL as long as they are on U.S. Title 10 or 32 (502)F Active Orders. The member must complete all phases of the credential (i.e. Funding Request, Funding for Exam, Taking the Exam) prior to orders expiring."
ang_eligibility.quote_opened_source_note: 460th Force Support Squadron (Buckley SFB) AF COOL trifold, PDF created 2024-07-05. A unit FSS publication, not the AF COOL office itself.
ang_eligibility.quote_official_fact_sheet_UNOPENED: "It includes all enlisted Air Force Specialty Codes (AFSCs) for activated Air National Guard Service members on Title 32 orders. Funding will be provided for ANG members on Title 32 (502F) active duty orders. Service members on Title 32 orders must be eligible for Title 10 benefits or operating under Title 10 authority." Also: "Air National Guard Service members on Drill Status are not eligible for AF COOL."
ang_eligibility.verification_status: UNVERIFIED by direct open: this wording came from search-engine extracts of the official page; the page could not be opened (host does not resolve from this network). Confirm on a .mil-reachable network or with the unit education office / AF COOL office (CCAF.AFCOOL.Reimb@us.af.mil per fact sheet).

ang_not_on_orders.value: Older sources say ANG/AFR members not on Title 10 orders may get funding from their own component. UNVERIFIED (only an undated Fairchild AFB article seen in search results, not opened).

va_licensing_certification_test_reimburs.name: GI Bill licensing and certification test reimbursement (VA)
va_licensing_certification_test_reimburs.what_it_pays: "We'll pay you back for the cost of the test, including registration and administrative fees." Cap: "no more than $2,000 per test." Only GI Bill-approved tests qualify, for as many tests as remaining entitlement and time limit allow.
va_licensing_certification_test_reimburs.test_fees_only: "We won't pay for fees or costs related to getting the actual license or certification document."
va_licensing_certification_test_reimburs.entitlement_charge: "We'll charge your entitlement based on the amount we paid back to you."
va_licensing_certification_test_reimburs.ang_relevance: Chapter 1606 (Selected Reserve) is listed, so a drilling ANG member who is eligible for Ch 1606 can use it. Individual eligibility for Ch 1606 / Ch 33 is not verified here.
va_licensing_certification_test_reimburs.condition: The test must be for a job that requires a license or certification (per VA page).

other_funding_sources.name: FAA / JSAMTCC Airman Knowledge Testing Program (free FAA mechanic knowledge tests)
other_funding_sources.value: FAA MOA lets JSAMTCC administer FAA airman knowledge tests to eligible groups including "Active-duty, cadets (service academy), guard, and reserve component personnel of the United States (U.S.) Air Force...". The 2A3X3 CFETP says the program lets military AMTs "take their written exams (general, airframe, and/or powerplant) at no cost to the member." FAA FAQ: "The FAA does not provide reimbursement of testing fees" at commercial centers.
other_funding_sources.covers: FAA AMT knowledge (written) tests only; oral/practical tests with a Designated Mechanic Examiner are not covered by this program (cost UNVERIFIED).

other_funding_sources.value: UNVERIFIED for ANG. Not researched to an official source; believed Army-only. Do not list as an ANG funding source without verification.

credentials.full_name: FAA Aviation Mechanic Certificate with Airframe and/or Powerplant ratings
credentials.exam_fee_note: Varies. FAA: knowledge test prices are set by the commercial testing centers (PSI); not published by FAA. Military/Guard members can take the three knowledge tests at no cost through FAA/JSAMTCC. Oral and practical test fees are set by the Designated Mechanic Examiner: UNVERIFIED.
credentials.prerequisites: 14 CFR 65.71: at least 18, read/write/speak/understand English, pass all tests within 24 months. 14 CFR 65.77: AMT school certificate, OR documented 'At least 18 months of practical experience' for one rating, OR 'At least 30 months of practical experience concurrently performing the duties appropriate to both the airframe and powerplant ratings.' Must pass knowledge, oral and practical tests (three knowledge tests). AF CFETP: Airmen may enroll in the AF A&P program once awarded the 5-skill level.
credentials.roles_source: CFETP 2A3X3 para 10.4.3 ('airlines, fixed-base operators, manufacturers, repair stations, aviation maintenance schools and in business or general aviation')
